docs.title: Vigie, a verified RAG assistant
docs.text: An assistant on digital finance (GDPR, MiCA, PSD2, AI Act, savings) that answers only from 115 official documents, cites its sources and refuses when it doesn't know. Everything runs locally. (C++20, RAG, SQLite FTS5, llama.cpp, evaluation)

docs.title: Vigie, a verified RAG assistant
docs.text: Keyword search (SQLite FTS5) and semantic search (bge-m3), rank fusion, reranking (bge-reranker-v2-m3), then an answer drafted by Qwen3.5-4B from 3 numbered passages. Below a relevance threshold, Vigie says the information isn't in its sources.

docs.title: Vigie, a verified RAG assistant
docs.text: Before showing an answer, Vigie checks that every citation exists and that every number appears in the cited passages. Otherwise it shows the passages as they are.

docs.title: Vigie, a verified RAG assistant
docs.text: 86 questions, including a hold-out set written after the model was chosen and never used for tuning: 18 of 18 out-of-scope questions refused, 62 drafted answers for 68 in-scope questions, 3 of them wrong on manual review.

docs.title: From data to robust surgery schedules
docs.text: How uncertain is the length of an operation, and what does learning that uncertainty change in an operating-room schedule? A small research study on 6,385 open surgeries. (Python, scikit-learn, conformal prediction, HiGHS (MILP), research)

docs.title: From data to robust surgery schedules
docs.text: Operating-room schedules rely on predicted durations, but the uncertainty around them is usually replaced by a fixed margin. Can it be learned from data, and does it make better schedules?

docs.title: From data to robust surgery schedules
docs.text: Gradient boosting predicts the time in the operating room (46 min mean error against 51 for the procedure's history). Historical 10th-90th percentiles cover only 76.5% of new cases; conformalized quantile regression covers 80.1% and has the best interval score in 10 of 10 random splits. Coverage still drops in small contexts such as robotic surgery.

docs.title: From data to robust surgery schedules
docs.text: An exact mixed-integer model (set packing, solved with HiGHS) fills four 8-hour rooms; each plan is replayed with the real durations. Planning every case at its learned 80th percentile cuts overtime from 113 to 19 minutes per room and day, with more utilisation than a uniform 15% buffer.

docs.title: From data to robust surgery schedules
docs.text: A budgeted robust model built on the learned deviations was too conservative: it protects against the worst deviations happening together, which rarely occurs.

docs.title: Road accidents in France and Haut-Rhin
docs.text: 310,000 injury accidents and 18,356 deaths, 2019 to 2024: when, where and to whom road deaths happen, and what turns a crash into a death. (Python, SQL (DuckDB), pandas, statsmodels, open data)

docs.title: Road accidents in France and Haut-Rhin
docs.text: Loaded 24 yearly files from the national police accident file (ONISR) whose format changes from year to year, and cleaned them into four tables with SQL in DuckDB. My death counts match the official figures exactly for 2019 to 2023.

docs.title: Road accidents in France and Haut-Rhin
docs.text: About 3,000 deaths a year, flat since 2019. Two thirds of them happen outside towns, which hold only a third of accidents. E-scooter deaths rose from 11 to 47 a year. Haut-Rhin is the 11th safest of 96 departments (36 deaths per million inhabitants against 46 nationally).

docs.title: Road accidents in France and Haut-Rhin
docs.text: A logistic regression on 17 risk factors: a pedestrian, a heavy vehicle, a fixed obstacle or a head-on collision multiply the odds of a death by 2.5 to 3 (AUC 0.76 on unseen data).

docs.title: Road accidents in France and Haut-Rhin
docs.text: Mulhouse records fewer accidents than Colmar, a smaller city, and 15 times fewer than Strasbourg. Minor accidents are under-recorded there, so only death-based indicators are reliable for this area.

docs.title: What France reimburses
docs.text: EUR 160 billion of medicines dispensed in pharmacies, 2019 to 2025: spending rose 43% while the number of boxes stayed flat. (Python, SQL (DuckDB), pandas, open health data)

docs.title: What France reimburses
docs.text: Loaded Open Medic (national health insurance) files with French number formats and mixed encodings into DuckDB, and checked that totals match to the euro across three levels of detail. Linked molecules that changed ATC code or spelling with a union-find algorithm (19% of spending).

docs.title: What France reimburses
docs.text: Reimbursements went from EUR 19.1 bn to 27.4 bn with the same number of boxes: new, expensive treatments drive the growth, with cancer and immunology drugs explaining EUR 3.2 bn. Patients on GLP-1 analogues more than doubled; adults treated for ADHD with methylphenidate rose from 17,000 to 114,000.

docs.title: What France reimburses
docs.text: People over 60 cost almost eight times more per head than under-20s. With direct age standardisation, Île-de-France moves from 11th to 3rd of 12 regions; Grand Est ranks 4th.

docs.title: Drone over Mulhouse
docs.text: A drone simulator over a 3D Mulhouse generated from national map data, which also produces labelled images of damaged buildings. (Unity 6, C#, HDRP, IGN open data, Python)

docs.title: Drone over Mulhouse
docs.text: Unity downloads about 90,000 building records, 22,500 street segments, rivers and railways from IGN, then generates the city: Alsatian roof styles, façades with windows and shutters up close, sidewalks and bridges. Trees are found by scanning 20 cm aerial photos for dark-green patches. An earthquake mode cuts buildings into pieces that fall under physics.

docs.title: Drone over Mulhouse
docs.text: Each capture is saved twice, before and after, with a pixel label image (11 classes: intact building, minor or major damage, destroyed, blocked road…). That is training data for damage-assessment models, which is hard to collect from real disasters.

docs.title: Drone over Mulhouse
docs.text: The first version ran in the browser (CesiumJS, TypeScript, webcam gestures). Image quality hit a ceiling, so I rebuilt it in Unity. The ruins are still not photorealistic, which could bias a model trained on them.

docs.title: Drone over Mulhouse
docs.text: Vary lighting and seasons per capture, and measure how a model trained on synthetic images does on real aerial photos.

docs.title: Nearest restaurant with Voronoi
docs.text: Click anywhere to find the closest restaurant. The Voronoi cell answers the question; Delaunay neighbours give the alternatives. (Python, VTK, pytest, computational geometry)

docs.title: Nearest restaurant with Voronoi
docs.text: Each restaurant owns the region of the map that is closer to it than to any other (its Voronoi cell). Finding your restaurant means finding your cell. Its Delaunay neighbours are the natural second choices. The original app adds filters by cuisine, rating and price, and lets you walk the user around with the arrow keys.

docs.title: Nearest restaurant with Voronoi
docs.text: 20 pytest tests, and a comparison of three methods (Voronoi cell, walking the Delaunay triangulation, brute force) on up to 5,000 random restaurants.

docs.title: Nearest restaurant with Voronoi
docs.text: Geometry turns a search over every point into a local question. The brute-force method is fine at 50 restaurants and clearly loses at 5,000.

docs.title: Boids and Flow-Lenia
docs.text: Flocking from three local rules, and a continuous cellular automaton whose creatures conserve their mass, computed on the GPU. (Unity 6, C#, compute shaders, emergence)

docs.title: Boids and Flow-Lenia
docs.text: Each boid only looks at its neighbours: keep some distance, match their heading, stay close to the group. Nothing tells the flock where to go, yet it moves as one. The Unity version adds obstacles, a predator, live tuning and a step-by-step debug mode. Move your pointer over the canvas to play the predator.

docs.title: Boids and Flow-Lenia
docs.text: A second scene runs Flow-Lenia (Plantec et al.) in a compute shader: matter climbs an affinity map and moves by reintegration tracking, so the total mass stays constant. Nine presets and a notebook to save the creatures you find.

docs.title: Boids and Flow-Lenia
docs.text: Neighbour search dominates the cost. A uniform grid keeps a thousand boids smooth.

docs.title: Membrana
docs.text: An artificial-life world where cells are membranes full of Flow-Lenia matter, and endosymbiosis can emerge without a rule forcing it. (C++20, Qt 6, OpenMP, CSV experiments)

docs.title: Membrana
docs.text: Each individual is a closed Fourier curve that encloses its own medium. Collisions are the only genetic event: fusion, inclusion or contact. A cell swallowed by another can be digested, or survive and be passed on to its host's descendants.

docs.title: Membrana
docs.text: The same engine runs with a GUI or headless. Headless runs write metrics, events and full lineages to CSV, and ablation campaigns (5 conditions × 5 seeds) remove one law at a time to see what it was responsible for. Mass is conserved to a relative error of 10⁻¹³, checked by tests.

docs.title: Membrana
docs.text: At first every membrane slowly emptied itself: outgoing flux always won. I added a nutrition law, which made permeability a real trade-off: better fed, but leakier.

docs.title: Membrana
docs.text: Compare evolutionary activity with the Flow-Lenia paper, and port the transport step to the GPU.

docs.title: Plagiarism checker
docs.text: A client sends a text over TCP; the server compares it with its library and returns a similarity report. (C, TCP sockets, text similarity)

docs.title: Plagiarism checker
docs.text: Texts are split into lowercase words, then into runs of three consecutive words. The plagiarism score is the share of the submitted text's three-word runs found in a reference text. Two Jaccard indices give context: shared vocabulary (same topic?) and shared phrases (same wording?).

docs.title: Plagiarism checker
docs.text: HELLO, then FICHIER with the size and name, then the bytes, then a multi-line report ending with FIN. Works on Windows (Winsock) and Linux.

docs.title: Plagiarism checker
docs.text: Shared vocabulary alone is misleading: two texts on the same subject share words without copying. Three-word runs separate the two cases well.

docs.title: Moving centres (k-means)
docs.text: Clustering by moving centres, with the distance and assignment steps parallelised with OpenMP. (C++, OpenMP, clustering)

docs.title: Moving centres (k-means)
docs.text: Pick k centres, assign each point to the nearest, move each centre to the mean of its points, repeat until nothing moves. The C++ version parallelises the distance matrix and the assignment over points.

docs.title: Moving centres (k-means)
docs.text: Filling the groups stays sequential on purpose: two threads pushing into the same vector at once is a race condition. Each thread only writes to its own cells.

docs.title: Moving centres (k-means)
docs.text: Change k, reshuffle, and step through iterations. Poor starting centres can split one blob in two and leave another merged.

docs.title: NSGA-III, explained
docs.text: Presenting Deb and Jain's NSGA-III paper and running its C++ implementation on DTLZ and ZDT benchmarks. (C++, multi-objective optimisation, team of 4)

docs.title: NSGA-III, explained
docs.text: One step of the algorithm, explained three times: in the paper, in the code, and in the experimental results.

docs.title: NSGA-III, explained
docs.text: The code ran, but its ZDT1 setup read the number of objectives as the number of variables, which made the problem far too easy. Two problems had no reference front, so their quality score (IGD) was meaningless.

docs.title: Vehicle-to-vehicle channels
docs.text: Simulating 2,000+ cars on Mulhouse's real road network and giving them radio channels by colouring the interference graph. (C++17, Qt 6, OpenStreetMap, Scrum)

docs.title: Vehicle-to-vehicle channels
docs.text: Cars that are close enough interfere, so they need different channels: that is graph colouring, re-run as cars move. We compare greedy, DSATUR, tabu search and incremental recolouring on quality, speed and how often cars must change channel.

docs.title: Vehicle-to-vehicle channels
docs.text: The map, zone selection and vehicle rendering work and are tested with 2,000 points. The engine is being connected. The benchmark campaign is planned for December.

docs.title: Hulls, maps and triangulations
docs.text: Incremental convex hull, combinatorial maps with half-edges, and incremental triangulation that handles aligned points. (C++, computational geometry)

docs.title: Hulls, maps and triangulations
docs.text: Written from scratch with a circular doubly linked polygon and half-edge maps, with a 34-page write-up of every function. Aligned points were the hard case in the triangulation.
